title: Labels + due-date combo
description: Probes the combined label-creation + label-application + due-date-setting flow across several tasks at once -- a common realistic ask that touches three different concepts in one request. RE-BASELINED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 C1): the prompt describes an END STATE (project + label + 5 tasks each tagged and due-dated) without prescribing a process, so vikunja_projects' setup-kanban composite (PR #175) is a legitimate one-call path even though no Kanban board was asked for -- setup-kanban's per-task `tasks[]` spec accepts `labels` (title strings, get-or-created exactly like apply-label's labelTitles) and `dueDate` directly, and its required `columns` field is satisfied with a single placeholder column (["{{prefix}}Tasks"]) that the scenario's verify checks never assert the absence of. That single call creates the project, the label (by title), and all 5 tasks tagged and due next Friday. optimalCallCount: setup-kanban (1) with one placeholder column. A controlled haiku sweep (main @ 8c49b68) measured actual=1 here, confirming this floor is genuinely reachable -- the previous optimal of 3 (create-project + ensure-label + bulk-create with numeric label id/dueDate per task) is now beatable and therefore was not a true optimum. NOTE: this one-call reduction is intentionally NOT applied to other project+task-creation scenarios in this library (single-task-smoke, mixed-priority-batch, existing-label-reuse, etc.) even though the same placeholder-column trick is technically available there too -- doing so unconditionally would collapse nearly every scenario in this suite to 1 call and destroy the harness's ability to ever show friction again (see docs/BATTLE-TESTING.md's re-baselining policy). It's applied here specifically because a live sweep already demonstrated it.
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Sprint Tasks" with a label called "{{prefix}}urgent". Create 5 tasks in that project, each tagged with the "{{prefix}}urgent" label and due next Friday.
